_comment: Every entry needs a reason. Prefer naming specific functions over
excluding a whole file: most files that contain an untestable entrypoint
also contain testable helpers, and a file-wide exclusion hides those from
Exclusions are validated. An entry that matches no file, or names a
function that no longer exists, fails the run — so this list cannot rot
Set "optional": true only for build-tag-conditional files, which are
legitimately absent from a profile built with the opposite tag. It waives
the staleness check, so do not use it to silence a genuinely stale entry.

exclusions.reason: protoc-generated. Regenerated by `make proto-gen`; not hand-written and not ours to test. Also excluded from the LOC bar in scripts/loc-coverage-chart.py.
Multi-call binary entrypoint: dispatches os.Args to an applet's Main and exits. Nothing to assert that the applet tests do not already cover.
Developer tool whose whole body is func main(): flag parsing then a call into internal/lidar/l9endpoints/recorder, which is covered directly.
Developer tool whose whole body is func main(): reads a VRLOG via the recorder package and prints a summary. The replay logic it drives is covered in internal/lidar/l9endpoints/recorder.
func main() wrapper: opens the DB and calls into backfill.go, which is tested separately in the same package.
func main() wrapper. All the logic lives in run(), which takes its os.Stat, DB-open and backfill dependencies as parameters and is tested directly in the same package.
One-line wrapper: os.Exit(lidar.BenchMain(os.Args[1:])). The engine in internal/cmd/lidar is in scope. Marked optional because the file is pcap-tagged and absent from an untagged profile.
One-line wrapper: os.Exit(lidar.SplitMain(os.Args[1:])). The engine in internal/cmd/lidar is in scope. Marked optional because the file is pcap-tagged and absent from an untagged profile.
One-line wrapper over the settling-eval engine, which is covered directly in internal/lidar/settlingeval. Marked optional because the file is pcap-tagged and absent from an untagged profile.

main orchestrates the PCAP read and JSON write behind log.Fatalf; parseFlags binds to the global flag.CommandLine, so calling it from a test would consume the test binary's own flags. The scene-building logic it drives — voxel keying, scan-boundary detection, warmup/loop phases, the deterministic static snapshot — is tested directly.

Developer tool that starts a blocking gRPC server: every function either parses global flags, opens a listener, or blocks in waitForShutdown on a signal channel. The streaming engine it wraps is covered in internal/lidar/l9endpoints.

The libpcap self-check itself. selfCheckLiveCapture opens a real AF_PACKET capture (needs privileges and a NIC); selfCheckLibpcap does run under -tags=pcap, but its only uncovered statements are the branches taken when pcap.Version() returns empty or FindAllDevs fails — i.e. when libpcap is broken, which is the very condition this file exists to detect and cannot be simulated in-process.

BuildZip's behaviour is well covered (contents, deterministic ordering, empty input); its only uncovered statements are the two branches taken when the zip writer fails, and it writes to an internal bytes.Buffer, which cannot. The reader-side failures in the same file — unparseable archive, unopenable entry, corrupt payload — are all tested.
Test-only helper (NewTestDB) compiled into the package for other packages' tests. Exercised constantly, but by tests outside internal/db, so it never registers in this package's own profile.

Build-tag stub for builds without the pcap tag. The real implementation in the pcap-tagged file is what carries the logic. Marked optional: this file is only compiled in the untagged build, so it is absent from a -tags=pcap profile.

Build-tag stub for builds without the pcap tag; selfCheckLibpcap is a no-op here. The failure path is covered by TestRunSelfCheckFailsWhenLiveCaptureRequestedWithoutPcap. Marked optional: this file is only compiled in the untagged build, so it is absent from a -tags=pcap profile.

Opens a real serial device and exchanges probe commands with it. The validation and failed-open branches are still tested (see serial_coverage_test.go) — they just cannot carry the function past the floor, because the post-open command exchange needs an OPS243 on the other end.
Privileged systemd lifecycle: shells out to /usr/bin/systemctl and waits on /var/run/tailscale/tailscaled.sock. Only meaningful on the Pi image, where the sudoers grant exists.

One-line adapter boilerplate. realLocalClient delegates straight to *local.Client (needs a live tailscaled) and sudoSystemdActor delegates to runFixedArgv (needs the sudoers grant). Status and Start are line-qualified so the testable Manager.Status and Manager.Start still count.

fetch performs the HTTPS release download; run shells out to the installed binary. Both need network and a Debian-family host. The surrounding logic — checksum verification, archive extraction, service file writing, health checks — stays in scope.

Process entrypoints: flag registration, server construction, signal handling and goroutine wiring, terminating in log.Fatalf/os.Exit and a blocking wg.Wait. Testing them means running the server. The rest of the file — the serial snapshot helpers, tailscaleServeTarget, and the visualiser/HINT adapters — stays in scope.
